D008-D011_h022.question:
I’ve been kind of all over the place for the past few months—like, the last two months especially, I was wired. Couldn’t sit still during meetings, even while code was deploying. I’d snap at my team over tiny delays, and I bought three new laptops and a smart home setup I don’t need. Burned through like four months of savings. I told myself I was optimizing my workflow, but honestly, I just felt restless, like my body wouldn’t let me shut off.

Then before that, for about three months, it was the opposite. Waking up at 4 a.m. every day, heart racing, but my head felt thick—like trying to run a virtual machine with no RAM. I’d stare at my desktop, unable to start anything, even emails. I kept thinking, *What’s the point of pushing commits if nothing really matters? I’d rather just not wake up tomorrow.* Not that I’d do anything, just… tired of existing. 

Now? I’m somewhere in the middle, but the anxiety’s always humming—sometimes it feels like the racing thoughts come from worry, sometimes they just *happen*. Can’t tell what’s driving what anymore.
D008-D011_h022.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D008-D011_h022.answer: C & A. Bipolar I Disorder & Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D008-D011_h023.question:
I’ve been struggling for about five months now—things just feel out of control. The first couple of months, I couldn’t sit still, like my body was buzzing. I’d clean the apartment at 3 a.m., start three projects at once, or call people I haven’t talked to in years. I felt on top of the world one minute, then snapped at a student over nothing the next. I even hooked up with someone from a bar—never done that before. No real reason, just felt like I needed *something*.  

Then it shifted. Around three months ago, I started staying in bed all weekend, avoiding calls—even from my sister. I wake up at 4 a.m. most nights and just lie there, heart racing. I can’t decide simple things—what to eat, what to wear. Last month, I filled a bottle with pills but didn’t take them. Just kept them in case.  

I’m still teaching, barely, but I’m exhausted. My mind races, but I don’t know if it’s from not sleeping, or worrying, or just… momentum. Sometimes I feel restless because I’m anxious. Other times, I don’t feel anxious at all—just driven. I can’t tell what’s causing what.
D008-D011_h023.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D008-D011_h023.answer: C & A. Bipolar I Disorder & Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D008-D011_h024.question:
The past few months have been… chaotic. I’d say it started around spring—after we expanded the shop. At first, I felt amazing, like I could work nonstop. I redesigned the entire storefront overnight, took on three weddings at once, and even invested $15,000 in a pop-up greenhouse idea I barely researched. I felt unstoppable, high, like everything sparkled. But then, just as suddenly, that flipped. I started snapping at customers over nothing. Little things—like picking stems—would infuriate me.

Then it all crashed. For maybe three months, I couldn’t enjoy anything. Not arranging flowers, not dinner with my husband, not even our garden. I’d wake up at 3 a.m. every night, heart racing, just staring at the ceiling. Choosing what to wear felt impossible—like each decision carried enormous weight. Lately… I’ve thought about how easy it would be to disappear. I’ve imagined driving into the mountains, stopping where there’s no cell signal… what kind of pills I might take. But I don’t want to die, not really. I just don’t know how to stop feeling like this. Everything shifts so fast—I can’t trust my own mind.
D008-D011_h024.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D008-D011_h024.answer: C & A. Bipolar I Disorder & Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D008-D011_h025.question:
Lately, I just feel like I’m on a rollercoaster I can’t get off. For about two months, I’d wake up at 3 a.m. buzzing—like my brain was sprinting. I’d clean the house, draft business plans for a skincare line, even wired money to reserve a domain name and lease space I never looked over. I felt brilliant, invincible—then, by noon, I’d snap at my husband over nothing and retreat.  

Then, everything crashed. For the next three months, getting dressed felt like climbing a mountain. I stopped checking my practice emails. Awards I’d worked years for? They meant nothing. I lie awake for hours, mind jumping between old regrets and how tired I am of existing. Last week, I stood in the garage staring at the car’s tailpipe… I’d pictured how it might happen, the timing, when the kids would be at school.  

I try to focus during appointments, but sentences blur. I’ll catch myself zoning out mid-consult. I don’t know if it’s anxiety building—or just this numb, chaotic fog. Sometimes I’m too keyed up to sit, other times I don’t care to move. It’s like I’m losing myself in shifts.
D008-D011_h025.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D008-D011_h025.answer: C & A. Bipolar I Disorder & Generalized Anxiety Disorder
